annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, and reciprocal condition-certificate formalization

assumptions: The positive scalars alpha and beta are lower and upper singular-value margins.
QA and Q preserve Euclidean norm, as thin QR factors do.
The exact QR algebra gives C*T=Q, and the square map T is surjective.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P07 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P07 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p07_t3_sketch_precondition_condition_certificate {m n s : Nat} (QA : Fin m -> Fin n -> Real) (Q C : Fin s -> Fin n -> Real) (T : Fin n -> Fin n -> Real) (alpha beta : Real) ... : (p07ConditionCertificate (QA*T) alpha beta iff p07ConditionCertificate C beta^-1 alpha^-1) and beta/alpha = alpha^-1/beta^-1
formal_statement.plain_language: The preconditioned matrix and the sketched orthonormal basis have reciprocal singular-value intervals and therefore the same condition ratio.

informal_proof: Use QA's isometry to identify the norm of QA*T*x with that of T*x. Write every vector as T*x, use C*T=Q and Q's isometry, and multiply the two certificate inequalities by the positive reciprocals. Reverse the argument and simplify the ratio algebra.
informal_statement: A finite all-threshold certificate version of the condition-number identity kappa_2(AP)=kappa_2(SQ_A) in Lemma 2.1.
